ledger.note: 1013: the Birzalids found the taifa of Carmona. The page: 'existed for two distinct periods: first from 1013 to 1066', 'established and ruled by the Zenata Berber Birzalid dynasty' under Abdallah ibn Ishaq al-Berzali (1013/4-1023/4); its infobox dates the kingdom 'c. 1037' and the Caliphate's downfall 1013.

1066: Seville conquers Carmona. The first taifa ended in 1066, 'when it was conquered by the Taifa of Seville'; the city page has the Abbadids conquer it 'by 1067', and the Taifa overview table gives Carmona 1013-1091 'to Seville' (a Seville that was Almoravid from 1091). Cliopatria keeps a Carmona shape to 1071. The first taifa ends here under al-'Aziz (1052/3-1066/7); the state is drawn again from c. 1143.

ledger.note: c. 1143: Carmona is a taifa again. The page has the second period 'from around 1143 to 1150' after the Almoravid rule of 1091-1143 in the infobox; it names no ruler and no land beyond the capital, so the circle round Carmona is the researcher's reading.

Reviewer eu-12-g (2026-10-25): Ibn Hamusk and 1161 are from the Carmona, Spain page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmona,_Spain: 'It was briefly occupied by Ibn Hamusk, before reverting to the Almohads in 1161'); the Taifa page does not mention him.

certainty.note: The pages name only the capital; no frontier, district or area is given. The first-period outline is Cliopatria's and the second is a circle round Carmona.

notes: Cliopatria rows: 1066-1071 draws a Carmona state after Seville's conquest; 1147-1151 is displaced (it does not contain Carmona) and runs a year past the Almohad conquest of 1150; the first shapes cannot be checked (no area, no town list on the page). The three pages disagree on the end of the first taifa: 1066 (Taifa of Carmona page and infobox), by 1067 (Carmona city page), 1091 (Taifa overview table, which lumps it with Seville's own end). The page budget (5) was not exhausted, but the Birzalids have no Wikipedia article under 'Birzalids' (not found); a gap-filler could try 'Banu Birzal' or the Spanish Wikipedia for Écija, Morón and the districts held by Carmona, and for the second taifa's ruler (the Taifa overview table says its dates and fate are uncertain). Mirrors needed: Seville (gain 1066), almoravid-dynasty (loss c. 1143), almohad-caliphate (gain 1150). Gazetteer name needed: Carmona (place, Sevilla province, 37.47 N 5.64 W), Écija.
